dossier.purpose: Python framework and `inspect` CLI for running large-language-model evaluations, created by the UK AI Security Institute (README.md:3); SECURITY.md:5 says Meridian Research Labs maintains it. An evaluation is a Task: a dataset of labelled Samples (input/target) + a solver or agent + one or more scorers (docs/index.qmd:87-93). In the repo: built-in solvers, tools, model graders and metrics; MCP client tools; Docker and local sandboxes; in-process and in-sandbox agent bridges; an eval-set runner with retry/resume; a versioned eval-log format with per-sample scores and errors; an HTTP log viewer; a control channel; an ACP server. README.md is a short developer-setup note that defers to https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/ (not fetched); user docs were read from docs/*.qmd. Facts for the stated needs: (1) several scorers per Task are supported and each sample's scores are stored per scorer name in EvalSample.scores (src/inspect_ai/log/_log.py:456). (2) claude_code()/codex_cli()/gemini_cli() agents are not in this repo; the docs place them in the separate inspect-swe package (docs/tutorial.qmd:351-370); the repo provides sandbox_agent_bridge() plus a Claude-Code-only demo in examples/. 'Verifier' and 'trial' are not Inspect terms; the closest are Scorer and epochs. (3) No declarative CI regression gate for prompts/skills/agents was found in this repo: eval-set exit code reflects task status only (src/inspect_ai/_eval/evalset.py:1740), `inspect eval` exits 0 on a task error (docs/control-channel.qmd:64), and no metric-threshold option exists; the docs mention a separate Inspect Flow package with declarative specs (docs/eval-sets.qmd:155-165) that could not be inspected here.

claims.claim: Inspect is a framework for large language model evaluations created by the UK AI Security Institute.
Provides many built-in components, including facilities for prompt engineering, tool usage, multi-turn dialog, and model graded evaluations.
Extensions (e.g. new elicitation and scoring techniques) can be provided by other Python packages.
Includes a collection of over 200 pre-built evaluations ready to run on any model (details at inspect.aisi.org.uk/evals/).
Docs for coding agents: structured index at /llms.txt, user guide at /llms-guide.txt, and /llms-full.txt with API and CLI reference; any page as Markdown by appending .md to its .html path.
Development install: clone the repo, then pip install -e ".[dev]".

uv alternative: `uv sync --extra dev` from the checked-in uv.lock; dependencies remain declared in requirements*.txt and exposed through pyproject.toml; change the requirements file and refresh the lockfile rather than using `uv add`.
`make hooks` installs pre-commit hooks; `make check` runs linting/formatting; `make test` runs the tests (prefix with `uv run` in a uv environment).
The web UI lives in the git submodule src/inspect_ai/_view/ts-mono/; submodule steps are only needed for TypeScript/React frontend work.
Docs are built with Quarto after pip install -e ".[doc]" (cd docs; quarto render).

install.method: PyPI user install (README.md itself documents only developer installs)
Editable developer install from a clone (pip)
install.command:
git clone https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai.git
cd inspect_ai
pip install -e ".[dev]"

pip install -e ".[doc]"
cd docs
quarto render

install.method: Model provider SDK, needed to run evals against a hosted model (OpenAI shown; Anthropic, Google and HF variants are listed too)
Companion package providing claude_code(), codex_cli(), gemini_cli() agents (separate project, not in this repo)

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - every CI job runs on ubuntu-latest (.github/workflows/build.yml:248, and all other workflows); the package is pure Python ('Operating System :: OS Independent', pyproject.toml:178); amd64 glibc and musl sandbox-tools artifacts are pinned (src/inspect_ai/tool/_sandbox_tools_utils/SHA256SUMS:1-4). The workflows do not state the runner CPU architecture.
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no WSL2 statement in README, docs or code; the only mention is a browser-opening helper in scripts/release-sandbox-tools.sh:65-69.
platforms.macos_arm64: unknown - no explicit support statement and no macOS CI runner (all workflows use ubuntu-latest, e.g. build.yml:248). Indirect signals only: package classified OS Independent (pyproject.toml:178); docs mention the macOS mps device for the HF provider (docs/providers.qmd:1012) and macosx:// notifications (docs/intervention.qmd:170); the arm64 sandbox-tools artifacts are Linux binaries for containers (SHA256SUMS:3-4).
platforms.gpu: no (not required) - the core dependency list has no GPU package (requirements.txt); only optional local-inference providers use one: the HF provider auto-uses CUDA or mps if available (docs/providers.qmd:1012) and vLLM/SGLang need user-installed packages (docs/providers.qmd:1133-1142).

integrations.cli: `inspect` console script (pyproject.toml:186-187 -> inspect_ai._cli.main:main, src/inspect_ai/_cli/main.py:21-66) and `python -m inspect_ai` (src/inspect_ai/__main__.py:1-4). Subcommands registered at _cli/main.py:43-56: eval, eval-set, eval-retry, score, view (start/bundle/embed), log (list/dump/convert/schema/export-config/recover), ctl (task/sample/model/process/config), acp, list tasks, info, cache, sandbox cleanup, trace, download restic. eval/eval-set/eval-retry accept --json launch/done records and --detach (docs/control-channel.qmd:49-100). `inspect eval-set` exits 1 unless all tasks succeeded (src/inspect_ai/_cli/eval.py:1681-1682); `inspect eval` exits 0 even when a task errors (docs/control-channel.qmd:64; _cli/eval.py:2199-2204).
integrations.mcp: MCP client, not server: mcp_server_stdio/http/sse/sandbox connect models to external MCP servers (docs/tools-mcp.qmd:39-62; src/inspect_ai/tool/_mcp/); the `mcp` package is an optional dependency checked at use (src/inspect_ai/tool/_mcp/server.py:196-208; listed only in requirements-dev.txt:17). sandbox_agent_bridge(bridged_tools=[BridgedToolsSpec]) exposes host-side Inspect tools to sandboxed CLI agents as MCP tools (docs/agent-bridge.qmd:148-196). No MCP server exposing Inspect's own eval or log operations was found (no mcp.server/FastMCP imports under src/).
integrations.sdk_or_api: Python SDK: inspect_ai exports eval, eval_async, eval_set, eval_retry, score, Task, task, Epochs, view, edit_score, recompute_metrics (src/inspect_ai/__init__.py:5-59); subpackages scorer, solver, dataset, model, tool, agent, log, analysis (samples_df/evals_df/messages_df/events_df), hooks, approval, review, util. HTTP/IPC: the `inspect view` FastAPI log-viewer API (routes src/inspect_ai/_view/fastapi_server.py:212-641; schema src/inspect_ai/_view/inspect-openapi.json; default bind 127.0.0.1:7575, src/inspect_ai/_util/constants.py:12-13; optional Authorization-token middleware, fastapi_server.py:662-674; non-loopback bind refused without auth, _view/network.py:97-110); a control server on a Unix domain socket for `inspect ctl` (docs/control-channel.qmd:45; src/inspect_ai/_control/server.py:1703-1728); an ACP (Agent Client Protocol) server via --acp-server and `inspect acp` (docs/intervention.qmd:16-28).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: In this repo: sandbox_agent_bridge() starts a model proxy inside the sandbox (port 13131) that forwards OpenAI/Anthropic/Google API calls from a CLI agent to the Inspect model (src/inspect_ai/agent/_bridge/sandbox/bridge.py:49-100, 221-233; docs/agent-bridge.qmd:70-121). A demo claude_code() agent execs the real `claude --print --dangerously-skip-permissions` in the container (examples/evals_in_eval/claude.py:15-58; Dockerfile installs @anthropic-ai/claude-code, examples/evals_in_eval/Dockerfile:24) and is labelled 'a demonstration of the basic mechanics' (claude.py:1-3). No Codex CLI agent or example in the repo (bridge code only accommodates codex-cli wire behavior, e.g. src/inspect_ai/agent/_bridge/responses_impl.py:262). The named agents claude_code(), codex_cli(), gemini_cli() are documented as living in the separate inspect-swe package (docs/tutorial.qmd:349-370; docs/agents.qmd:14) and could not be inspected. Agent-facing tooling: `inspect eval --json/--detach` and `inspect ctl ... --json` are designed for coding agents (docs/control-channel.qmd:43-124); AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md just contains `@AGENTS.md`) and four contributor skills under .agents/skills/ (AGENTS.md:297-299); the companion inspect-skills plugin and llms.txt docs (docs/index.qmd:82; README.md:11) are not verifiable here; the skill() tool gives models Agent Skills inside a sandbox (docs/tools-standard.qmd:609-649).

readme.telemetry_and_network: No default telemetry, analytics or phone-home found in src/ (searches for telemetry/analytics/sentry/posthog hit only the opt-in items below). Opt-in only: the legacy env hook INSPECT_TELEMETRY=<module.function> sends model_usage, eval_log_location and eval_log events to the named provider, and INSPECT_API_KEY_OVERRIDE can read/modify API-key env vars; both are deprecated and a startup banner lists them when enabled (src/inspect_ai/hooks/_legacy.py:1-34, 50-98; src/inspect_ai/hooks/_startup.py:16-36); any installed package that registers an `inspect_ai` entry point is imported at startup (src/inspect_ai/_util/entrypoints.py:19-31). Required or likely network services and accounts: an API key and network access for the chosen model provider (docs/index.qmd:43-77; the mockllm provider needs none, src/inspect_ai/model/_providers/mockllm.py:15-25); Docker Engine + Compose for the docker sandbox (src/inspect_ai/util/_sandbox/docker/prereqs.py:28-100); Hugging Face for hf_dataset (docs/index.qmd:110). Runtime downloads: sandbox-tools binaries from the public S3 bucket inspect-sandbox-tools.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com when not bundled in the wheel (musl sandboxes, editable installs), SHA-256 checked against the vendored SHA256SUMS and rejected on mismatch (src/inspect_ai/tool/_sandbox_tools_utils/sandbox.py:63, 642-654, 685-727; CHANGELOG.md:171); the restic binary from github.com/restic/restic releases for checkpointing, checked against vendored sums (src/inspect_ai/util/_restic/resolver.py:47; src/inspect_ai/util/_restic/README.md:1-7); Docker Hub images aisiuk/inspect-tool-support and aisiuk/inspect-computer-tool (src/inspect_ai/util/_sandbox/docker/config.py:116; src/inspect_ai/tool/_tools/_computer/_common.py:360-364). Local services: `inspect view` binds 127.0.0.1:7575 by default and refuses a non-loopback bind without an authorization token or --unsafe-allow-unauthenticated (src/inspect_ai/_util/constants.py:12-13; src/inspect_ai/_view/network.py:97-110); the control channel is a Unix domain socket with a peer-UID check (docs/control-channel.qmd:45; src/inspect_ai/_control/server.py:259-273); the sandbox bridge proxy listens on loopback inside the sandbox and withholds web_search, code_execution and remote MCP unless granted (docs/agent-bridge.qmd:80, 125-134; src/inspect_ai/agent/_bridge/sandbox/bridge.py:155-163). Logs (inputs, outputs, tool calls) are written locally to ./logs or INSPECT_LOG_DIR by default (docs/eval-sets.qmd:43). CI only: docs rendering uses no API keys (.github/workflows/build.yml:166-171); sync_model_data.yml uses TOGETHER_API_KEY/FIREWORKS_API_KEY secrets weekly (.github/workflows/sync_model_data.yml:34-41).

code.architecture: Under src/inspect_ai unless noted. _cli/ (click app: eval.py, log.py, score.py, view.py, acp.py, ctl/) -> _eval/ (eval.py: eval/eval_async/eval_retry; evalset.py: eval_set with retry and sample reuse; score.py; task/task.py: Task; task/run.py: per-sample pipeline solver -> scorers -> EvalSample, with error/retry/limit handling). Building blocks: dataset/ (Sample; csv/json/hf sources), solver/ (TaskState, generate, prompt/multiple_choice/etc.), scorer/ (scorers, metrics, epoch reducers in _reducer/, Score incl. Score.unscored), agent/ (react, deepagent, human agent, _bridge/ in-process and sandbox bridges, _acp/ Agent Client Protocol), tool/ (standard tools, _mcp/ MCP client, _sandbox_tools_utils/ injection of the PyInstaller-built inspect-sandbox-tools binary), model/ (Model API plus ~50 provider modules in _providers/, including mockllm), util/_sandbox/ (SandboxEnvironment ABC with built-in docker/ and local providers; other providers are external packages), util/_checkpoint + util/_restic (checkpoint/resume), log/ (EvalLog/EvalSample models in _log.py, recorders for .eval/.json plus realtime buffer in _recorders/, recovery in _recover/, edits), _control/ (control-channel server for `inspect ctl`), _view/ (FastAPI log-viewer server; prebuilt UI in dist/, source in the ts-mono submodule), analysis/ (pandas dataframes), hooks/, approval/, review/, event/, _display/ (rich/textual/plain). Separate packages in-tree: src/inspect_sandbox_tools (tool server and model_proxy injected into containers) and src/inspect_tool_support (legacy container-image tools). Extensions from other pip packages load through the `inspect_ai` entry-point group (src/inspect_ai/_util/entrypoints.py:19).
code.packaging_and_release: Build: setuptools + setuptools_scm, version derived from git tags matching [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]* (pyproject.toml:1-21); wheel package data includes the prebuilt viewer (_view/dist), SHA256SUMS and sandbox_tools_version.txt (pyproject.toml:36-49); sdist trimmed by MANIFEST.in. PyPI release is a manual maintainer script, not a workflow: scripts/pypi-release.py (`python3 -m build` at :696, `twine upload` of dist/* at :719-724, tag pushed only after upload at :733-734; auth from ~/.pypirc or TWINE_USERNAME/TWINE_PASSWORD at :424-447; process documented in src/inspect_sandbox_tools/design/RELEASING.md:86-94). No GitHub Actions PyPI-publish workflow exists in .github/workflows (design/sandbox-tools-ci-gates.md:9 refers to a 'PyPI publish flow'). No signing, Sigstore, SLSA or PEP 740 attestation config and no published wheel/sdist checksums were found. Integrity controls that do exist: the four sandbox-tools artifacts (amd64/arm64 x glibc/musl, version 32) are pinned by SHA-256 in src/inspect_ai/tool/_sandbox_tools_utils/SHA256SUMS:1-4 and verified at runtime download (sandbox.py:685-727), in the release script's pre-build gate (pypi-release.py:282-324), in a post-build wheel-contents check (:327-352) and in the CI release gate (build.yml:596-641); upload_to_s3.py refuses to overwrite a published version with different bytes and round-trip verifies uploads (upload_to_s3.py:132-143, 173-182). Those PyInstaller binaries are built locally by maintainers with Docker and are not reproducible (BINARY_INTEGRITY.md:52-54; RELEASING.md:39-54); glibc builds are bundled in the wheel, musl builds are fetched from S3 at runtime (RELEASING.md:94). restic: pinned version plus vendored upstream SHA256SUMS (src/inspect_ai/util/_restic/README.md:1-7; authenticity check is a manual gpg step, :21-27). Other publish paths: .github/workflows/npm-publish.yml (tag push -> npm publish of the viewer library using Trusted Publishing/id-token, :4-7, 28-30, 99-101) and .github/workflows/docker.yml (manual dispatch -> multi-arch aisiuk/inspect-computer-tool and aisiuk/inspect-tool-support images to Docker Hub with no-cache, :1-86; no image signing found).
code.tests_and_ci: Framework: pytest (xdist, timeout, mock, cov, dotenv, reportlog, textual-snapshot) with anyio so every async test also has a trio variant (tests/conftest.py:36-55; pyproject.toml:98-115; requirements-dev.txt:30-39). Tests: ~642 test_*.py files under tests/ (subdirs _cli, _control, _eval, _util, _view, agent, analysis, approval, checkpoint, dataset, hooks, log, model, review, scorer, solver, timeline, tools, util, plus 44 top-level files), 18 under src/inspect_sandbox_tools/tests (own pytest config), 6 under src/inspect_tool_support and 2 other in-package files; ~800 tests call eval() (tests/conftest.py:216-217). Scoring and failure-handling tests include tests/scorer/test_multiscorer.py, tests/scorer/test_reducers.py, tests/test_score_on_error.py and tests/test_fail_on_error.py. Gated classes are skipped by default and the run still exits green: --runslow, --runapi (needs provider keys), --runflaky, --runtrio (tests/conftest.py:58-79, 938-954; .agents/skills/slow-tests/SKILL.md:8-25); PR CI runs no live-provider tests and only some slow areas; tests needing the ts-mono submodule skip when it is absent (tests/test_npm_publish_workflow.py:72). Workflows (.github/workflows, every job on ubuntu-latest): build.yml = ruff lint+format, mypy (py3.10/3.11), pre-commit (uv-lock, typos, yaml/json checks, private-key detection), docs render (Quarto, no code execution), test matrix py3.10/3.11 running `pytest -ra --doctest-modules -n logical --timeout=900 ...` (:350; skipped for docs-only changes, :286-298), sandbox-tools-unit, detect-slow -> check-version-bump -> slow-tool-tests-dev / slow-tool-tests-release (Docker, `pytest --runslow -m slow tests/tools/`, :517-655), slow-tests for the checkpoint area (:661-696), and package build+inspect via hynek/build-and-inspect-python-package (:698-728); log_viewer.yml = OpenAPI/schema drift, submodule-on-main, viewer tests, dist-up-to-date; suppressions.yml = ledger gate for noqa/type-ignore; changelog-lint.yml; pr-gate.yml (contribution-policy gate, enforcing); pr-stale.yml; suppressions-comment.yml; sync_model_data.yml (weekly PR); docker.yml and npm-publish.yml (publishing); test.yml is a stub. Local equivalents: `make check` (ruff, mypy, suppressions-check) and `make test` (Makefile:16-33).

code.security_policy: SECURITY.md (repo root): report privately by email to security@meridianlabs.ai, not via public issues (:5); acknowledgement within 3 business days, assessment within 10 business days, fix target 30 days (:16-18); fixes only for the latest PyPI release (:26); no bug bounty (:22); disclosure via GitHub security advisory and CVE where applicable (:51). In scope: code execution or file access from opening a log/dataset, Docker sandbox escape, secrets written to logs, flaws in the log viewer/server, release/packaging/CI flaws (:32-38). Out of scope: the `local` sandbox having no isolation, model code running in a sandbox, loading untrusted task/solver/scorer/config files (runs that code), Docker's limited isolation, third-party dependency bugs, scanner or LLM-generated reports without a working proof of concept (:40-47).

risks: Scope gap against the stated needs: the named Claude Code / Codex CLI agents live in the separate inspect-swe package, not this repo (docs/tutorial.qmd:351-370; docs/agents.qmd:14); the repo has only a Claude Code demo (examples/evals_in_eval/claude.py:1-3) and no Codex example, and no test launching the real claude or codex CLIs was found, so their behavior is not exercised by this repo's checks.

No built-in metric-threshold or regression gate: eval-set success is status-only (src/inspect_ai/_eval/evalset.py:1740), `inspect eval` exits 0 when a task errors (docs/control-channel.qmd:64; src/inspect_ai/_cli/eval.py:2199-2204), and fail_on_error counts sample errors only (docs/handling-errors.qmd:24-63). CI gating on scores for prompts, skills or agents needs custom code; the docs' declarative option (Inspect Flow, docs/eval-sets.qmd:155-165) is a separate package not inspectable here.

A green run does not mean covered: slow/api/flaky/trio tests are skipped by default and the run still exits green (tests/conftest.py:938-954; .agents/skills/slow-tests/SKILL.md:8-12); PR CI runs no live-provider tests and only tests/tools plus the checkpoint area of the slow tests (AGENTS.md:176-181; .github/workflows/build.yml:517-563, 661-696); submodule-dependent tests skip when ts-mono is absent (tests/test_npm_publish_workflow.py:72). Verifying a change needs explicit flags and a read of the -ra skip summary.

Pre-1.0 churn: version 0.3.275 with 16 releases between 21 Aug and 1 Oct 2026 (CHANGELOG.md:1, 353) and 'Development Status :: 4 - Beta' (pyproject.toml:169). Scorer results changed in a patch release (f1() now counts repeated tokens, 'scores can rise or fall', CHANGELOG.md:51) and an `inspect ctl` payload field changed incompatibly (CHANGELOG.md:98); deprecated APIs are slated for removal at 0.4 (src/inspect_ai/analysis/__init__.py:93-101).

Release provenance: PyPI publishing is a manual maintainer script using a PyPI token from ~/.pypirc or TWINE_* env vars (scripts/pypi-release.py:424-447, 696-724); no CI-built provenance, signatures or attestations and no published wheel checksums were found. The injected sandbox-tools binaries run inside sandboxes, are non-reproducible PyInstaller builds whose trust anchor is merge rights (src/inspect_sandbox_tools/design/BINARY_INTEGRITY.md:8-12, 47-54), and Docker Hub images are not digest-pinned (BINARY_INTEGRITY.md:58-59).

Code-execution surface by design: tasks, solvers, scorers and config files are Python that runs with the user's privileges; the `local` sandbox is unisolated and Docker gives limited isolation (SECURITY.md:30-47); every installed package with an inspect_ai entry point is imported at startup (src/inspect_ai/_util/entrypoints.py:19-31); INSPECT_API_KEY_OVERRIDE and INSPECT_TELEMETRY hooks can read keys or ship logs when set (src/inspect_ai/hooks/_legacy.py:19-34, 50-61); the Claude Code demo runs the CLI with --dangerously-skip-permissions (examples/evals_in_eval/claude.py:23).

Thin platform evidence: every workflow job runs on ubuntu-latest and tests run on Python 3.10/3.11 only (.github/workflows/build.yml:248, 255, 73); no macOS, Windows, WSL2 or arm64 host jobs, so macOS arm64 and WSL2 behavior is unverified upstream; the docker sandbox needs Docker Engine and Compose (src/inspect_ai/util/_sandbox/docker/prereqs.py:28-100).

Governance and maintenance: README names UK AISI while SECURITY.md:5 says Meridian Research Labs maintains Inspect; external PRs need a maintainer-accepted issue or are auto-closed (CONTRIBUTING.md:7-26; .github/workflows/pr-gate.yml:1-11, 41) and inactive PRs close after 60+7 days (.github/workflows/pr-stale.yml:27-28); security fixes cover only the latest PyPI release (SECURITY.md:26); some design docs lag the code (BINARY_INTEGRITY.md:203-211 vs sandbox.py:685-727); viewer source sits in a separate submodule repo (.gitmodules:1-3).
